scenes.title: Architectural wooden tabletop Trolley Switch vs Footbridge model beside Princeton's 2001 fMRI response console
scenes.era: 2001, Princeton University neuroimaging & moral cognition laboratory

layout.description: Sunlit academic laboratory featuring a clean white birch tabletop railway-junction diorama with two side-by-side miniature scenes — Track A with a brass-handled points switch lever diverting a wooden tram toward 1 figure away from 5 figures, and Track B with a miniature elevated footbridge above 5 figures — beside a dual-button response pad and reaction-time display.

positions.who: Joshua Greene (mannequin in 2001 collared shirt and crewneck sweater)
positions.where: standing beside the split wooden track diorama demonstrating the impersonal Switch lever on the left versus the elevated Footbridge figure on the right
seated with index fingers poised over 'Appropriate' and 'Inappropriate' response buttons — pressing instantly on Switch (~85% Yes) then hesitating 2 extra seconds on Footbridge

props.name: split wooden Trolley Switch vs Footbridge architectural model
props.period_detail: clean white-birch Y-junction track with mechanical switch lever on one side and elevated footbridge span with 5 vs 1 miniature porcelain figures on the other
props.physical_behavior: makes the identical 5-for-1 math vs opposite human action visually unmistakable

props.name: two-button moral response box & reaction-time timer ('4.9s No vs 6.8s Yes')
props.period_detail: white clinical button box wired to a crisp reaction-time bar display

actions.verb_sequence: flips the impersonal track switch lever on Model A -> Participant taps 'Appropriate' briskly -> shifts to the elevated Footbridge on Model B -> Participant's finger freezes in mid-air over the button for two tense seconds
pulls hand back to press 'Inappropriate' on Footbridge despite identical 5-vs-1 figures

reactions.reaction: stares between both models realizing the body count never changed — only personal muscular force changed
points to the diverging emotional vs working-memory response curves on the console

scenes.wardrobe: Early-2000s Princeton academic attire: collared button-down under fine-knit crewneck sweater, tailored trousers.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key New Jersey daylight across pale birch wood and matte-white porcelain.
scenes.recognition_hook: Five figures vs one figure on both tracks — yet flipping a switch feels obvious while touching one figure on a footbridge freezes the human hand.

key_visual.description: a wooden tabletop railway diorama contrasting a track switch lever and an elevated footbridge with five vs one miniature porcelain figures beside a two-button response box

scenes.title: The 2-Second Utilitarian Hesitation Under Cognitive Load

layout.description: Bright testing booth where a participant holds a 7-digit number strip in mind while evaluating Switch vs Footbridge cards.

positions.where: pausing noticeably longer on utilitarian overrides while gut 'No' presses stay fast

props.name: digit-load memory strip & timer
props.physical_behavior: proves utilitarian calculation requires executive bandwidth

actions.verb_sequence: memorizes 7 digits -> taps fast emotional 'No' -> slows markedly when computing utilitarian 'Yes'

reactions.reaction: logs selective slowing on utilitarian overrides alone

scenes.recognition_hook: Tie up working memory with seven digits, and ONLY cold utilitarian math slows down while the gut alarm fires at full speed.

scenes.title: Personal Muscular Force vs Remote Switch Control

layout.description: Clean tabletop comparing a trapdoor switch on the footbridge against direct hand contact.

positions.where: contrasting remote trapdoor lever vs direct push across four matched dilemma cards

props.name: 2x2 Personal Force × Intention card matrix
props.period_detail: isolates why direct muscular force as an intentional means trips the alarm

actions.verb_sequence: places remote-switch vs direct-force cards side by side -> approval rate drops sharply when muscular force is direct

scenes.recognition_hook: It isn't distance alone — it is using your own muscles to harm one person as a deliberate tool that trips the ancient alarm.

scenes.title: Auto-Mode vs Manual-Mode Triage in Real Policy
scenes.era: Modern hospital ethics & autonomous-vehicle safety boardroom

layout.description: Sunlit conference table where engineers and clinicians compare an individual case file beside a population safety chart.

positions.where: explicitly checking both compassionate bedside duties and transparent population-wide safety numbers

props.name: dual checklist ('Individual Rights Guardrail' + 'Total Lives Saved Math')
props.period_detail: keeps both neural cameras visible on the table
props.physical_behavior: prevents blind spots from either extreme

actions.verb_sequence: places both checklists side by side before finalizing emergency protocol

scenes.wardrobe: Modern medical coat and business-casual attire.
scenes.recognition_hook: Wise institutions honor the gut alarm that protects individuals while switching to manual mode when policy numbers affect thousands.
